verdict_reason: Routes, gating, token verification and error handling meet the AC; two Major code-quality items remain: a refused-token log with no search ids, and a second home for the unauthorised page render.

todos.issue: The ID-token refusal log ('IDM ID token refused', line 92) carries only { err }: no state, contactId, sessionId or correlationId, while the other two outcomes of the same handler log state (line 80) and contactId/sessionId/correlationId (lines 104-106). Support cannot tie a refused sign-in to the user or the IDM correlation id during an incident.
todos.fix: Must: the refused-token log line carries the ids support searches by for this sign-in (at least state and the IDM correlationId/contactId), alongside { err }. One way: decode the unverified ID token claims inside the catch (guarded, since decode itself can throw) and log contactId, sessionId, correlationId and request.query.state with err.

todos.issue: unableToSignIn (line 58) writes the view literal 'auth/unauthorised' and base(sharedCopy.unauthorised.title) again; src/server/auth/controller.js:9 already owns it as UNAUTHORISED_VIEW and renders the same view and title four times. Two homes for the unable-to-sign-in page render.
todos.fix: Must: one function owns rendering the unable-to-sign-in page (view name and title), taking the try-again link as a named option; controller.js and idm-sign-in.js both call it. One way: export a helper such as renderUnableToSignIn(h, { signInUrl }) from a shared auth module and use it in both files, removing the local constant and literal.
